scenes.narration: To everyone who keeps putting it off. Small steps still count.
The keeper climbed the same hill every morning. Nobody asked him to.
He trimmed the wick, cleaned the glass, and wrote one line in the log. Then he did it all again.
Years passed. Then one night a storm took the stars, and a ship lost its way.
The lamp was burning, as it had every night before. Because of one small habit, the ship came home.
So pick one small thing. Do it today. Do it again tomorrow.
Nobody may see it. It still counts.

brief.angle: A lighthouse keeper climbs the same hill every morning to trim the wick and clean the glass, with nobody watching. Years later a storm hides the stars and a lost ship finds its way home by his light. The small habit nobody saw is what saved it.
brief.lesson: Small steps still count, even when nobody sees them.
brief.audience: Someone who keeps putting off a thing because one small step feels too small to matter.
titles: One Small Habit, One Stormy Night
